A consonant in the bottom slot of a syllable is a 'batchim'. All final consonants collapse to one of 7 sounds: ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ, ㅁ, ㅂ, ㅇ. For example ㅅ, ㅈ, ㅊ, ㅌ, ㅎ at the end all sound like ㄷ (a stopped 't'). When the next syllable starts with ㅇ, the batchim moves over and is pronounced fully.
